title: Polish prosecutors charge fifth suspect in Zondacrypto investigation
dek: Polish authorities charged Roman Ż. with organized crime and misappropriation in connection with the collapsed Zondacrypto exchange (formerly BitBay). The exchange froze withdrawals in April, leaving 1.3 million clients locked out with approximately $94 million in estimated losses.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: A fifth suspect has been charged in Poland's ongoing investigation into Zondacrypto, a cryptocurrency exchange that collapsed after freezing customer withdrawals and leaving over a million users unable to access their assets.
bottom_line: The pretrial detention hearing for Roman Ż. will test the strength of Polish prosecutors' evidence; any conviction or plea would establish accountability in a case that has so far left 1.3 million customers without recourse.
body: Polish prosecutors have charged Roman Ż. with organized crime and misappropriation offenses in the Zondacrypto investigation, according to reporting by Cointelegraph and other outlets. Prosecutors are seeking pretrial detention for the suspect.

The charge marks an escalation in Poland's enforcement action against Zondacrypto, the exchange that collapsed after freezing customer withdrawals in April. The platform, which operated as BitBay until its 2021 rebrand, left approximately 1.3 million clients unable to access their accounts, with estimated losses of at least $94 million.

Zondacrypto's collapse is part of a broader pattern of exchange failures and alleged misconduct at the firm. According to Decrypt's reporting, two chief executives of the exchange have vanished four years apart, underscoring instability in the platform's leadership.

Polish prosecutors have now brought charges against multiple suspects as the investigation continues. The addition of this fifth suspect indicates the scope of the inquiry extends across the exchange's management and operations.
